title: KEDA scaledown sensitivity causes capacity cliff and cold-start surge
creator: Dana Chen
description: During a regional capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed an abrupt drop in available replicas for several model-serving pools. KEDA scaledowns triggered aggressively due to a combination of metric smoothing inversion and a misconfigured activation threshold, producing a capacity cliff and a surge in cold-start latency for live customers. This ticket documents the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and follow-up actions.
postmortem_summary: A bug in our custom metrics adapter introduced an inverted smoothing window for request latency, causing transient low-rate signals to be interpreted as steady low demand. KEDA ScaledObjects with a short cooldown and low activationThreshold scaled pods down too quickly. Result: underprovisioning during a short traffic spike and elevated p95/p99 generation latency. Immediate mitigations stabilized traffic; long-term fixes include metric adapter rollback, KEDA/HPA config hardening, and improved integration tests.

root_cause: A recent change (ENG-33011) to the metrics adapter unintentionally inverted the smoothing logic used to compute the time-weighted request rate. The inverted smoothing produced artificially low demand signals. KEDA ScaledObject configurations with aggressive scaledown settings (short cooldown and low activationThreshold) used those signals and scaled pods down prematurely, creating a capacity cliff during a short traffic spike.
contributing_factors: No canary for metrics-adapter changes against production KEDA ScaledObjects
ScaledObjects had a short stabilization window and low minReplicas, making them sensitive to transient metric errors
Alerting thresholds monitored raw request counts but not smoothed_rate, delaying detection of the metric adapter regression
Unit/integration tests did not cover the smoothing inversion edge case
mitigations_during_incident: Manual increase of minReplicas for affected Deployments to 6 (Marco Ruiz)
Rollback metrics-adapter to stable image tag (v2026-02-12-stable)
Temporarily increased KEDA pollingInterval on affected clusters from 30s to 60s to reduce oscillation
Enabled conservative autoscaler fallback: HPA target fallback to CPU-based metric for critical pools

Verify KEDA ScaledObjects do not scale below configured minReplicas during tests and that smoothed_rate tracks raw_rate within 10% on test traffic. After canary success, roll to production with 1% gradual rollout and monitor 'smoothed_rate vs raw_rate' dashboard and scaling behavior for 48h.
